Name: Ville de Paris — Permis de végétaliser
What they do: Lets groups (associations, schools, businesses, 5+ residents) plant on public space: tree bases, de-paved ground, planters. Charter: local and bee-friendly plants, no pesticides, no plastic, year-round care. 1,732 permits in open data.
Why relevant for EcoScape: The legal version of 'guerrilla gardening': EcoScape can be its digital front door.

Name: Parisculteurs
What they do: Calls for projects on rooftops, schoolyards and unused plots for urban agriculture (season 5 listed). Operator not named on site [À VÉRIFIER: City of Paris].
Why relevant for EcoScape: Pipeline of real edible-planting sites in Paris.

Name: La SAUGE
What they do: Runs or supports 6 urban farms in the Paris region, sells organic seeds, offers corporate solidarity days, training and volunteering. 2026 season active.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Hands-on planting partner and a ready-made corporate offer for sponsors.

Name: Halage
What they do: Green-space worksites for people far from employment; Fleurs d'Halage local flower production in Île-de-France; Lil'Ô biodiversity site. Urban-agriculture training Sept–Dec 2026.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Local, ethical supplier of pollinator flowers plus a strong social-impact story.

Name: botanic®
What they do: Garden-centre chain; removed synthetic pesticides and chemical fertilisers in 2008; société à mission since 2021; endowment fund for forests.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Natural sponsor and plant supplier; its no-pesticide line matches the permis charter.

Name: UNAF — Union Nationale de l'Apiculture Française
What they do: Represents French beekeepers; 'Abeille, sentinelle de l'environnement' programme; APIcité label for local authorities. Reports 90% of surveyed beekeepers oppose GPS location of hives.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Expert voice for the pollinator option. Design lesson: never geolocate hives in the app.

Name: Data For Good
What they do: Volunteer tech community (8,000 volunteers, 140 projects) on climate, social justice and democracy. Season 15 launches 7 Nov 2026.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Possible volunteer support and credibility on open data; timing fits our project.

Name: AFAUP — Association Française de l'Agriculture Urbaine
What they do: National urban-agriculture association; organises '48h de l'agriculture urbaine' (Apr 2026); manifesto 'Un quartier, une ferme'.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Relay to urban farms across France; event to launch a challenge.

Name: LPO — Refuges LPO
What they do: Refuges LPO: France's network of wildlife-friendly gardens, with tracks for individuals, companies and local authorities.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Label for planting sites; biodiversity credibility.

Name: CDC Biodiversité — Nature 2050
What they do: Nature 2050 co-finances nature-based solutions incl. urban climate adaptation; 10th anniversary in 2026.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Possible co-funding for heat-island plantings.

Name: Merci Raymond
What they do: Urban gardeners and designers: plant design, urban agriculture, maintenance, education (projects at La Villette, offices, campuses). No dated 2025-26 news on site.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Professional planting/maintenance operator for corporate sponsors.

Name: Kingfisher (Castorama, Brico Dépôt)
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international biodiversity commitments.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Retail sponsor with garden ranges.

Name: VINCI
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: BTP sponsor for de-paving (désimperméabilisation) plantings.

Name: Saint-Gobain
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Materials and construction sponsor; Stavian-like industrial profile.

Name: Bouygues Construction
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: BTP sponsor for urban sites.

Name: EDF
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Energy sponsor; heat/energy narrative.

Name: ENGIE
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Energy sponsor; heat/energy narrative.

Name: Carrefour
What they do: Signatory of act4nature international.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Distribution sponsor for the edible-garden option.

Name: Noé
What they do: Protects threatened species, builds a nature-friendly economy, reconnects people with nature; active 2026 (pesticides campaign).
Why relevant for EcoScape: Biodiversity credibility; corporate partnership programme.

Name: Reforest'Action
What they do: Since 2010, reforestation and regenerative agriculture projects funded by companies (650+ large companies). Mostly outside cities.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Benchmark/competitor (French Treedom-like model); shows why our urban, educational angle differs.

Name: Plantons pour l'Avenir
What they do: Since 2014, funds reforestation of French forests with 455 corporate sponsors.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Forest-focused, not urban: useful benchmark of corporate tree sponsorship in France.
